CVE-2026-129986.description: Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). Prior to 0.31.1, mount.deleteFileMount passes a path containing the user-controlled filePath to the local removeFileOrDirectory helper, which interpolates it unquoted into rm -rf, while the remote branch is quoted. An authenticated member with file-mount create and delete permissions can execute arbitrary commands in the host context immediately when deleting a local file mount, without requiring a running container. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.1.

CVE-2026-129316.description: Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). From 0.29.13 until 0.31.0, the Docker terminal, container-log, and monitoring WebSocket handlers accept a caller-controlled serviceId as authorization but do not consistently bind the requested containerId or appName to that service. A member with read access to any service can consequently target unrelated containers, obtain a root shell in the Dokploy panel container, read other tenants' logs and statistics, and use the mounted Docker socket to compromise the host. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.0.

CVE-2026-129991.description: Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). Prior to 0.31.1, the backup prefix field is only checked for a nonempty value, and normalizeS3Path preserves shell metacharacters before the prefix is interpolated into rclone upload and retention-cleanup command strings. An authenticated organization member with backup permission for a service can execute arbitrary commands as root on the Dokploy host or configured remote server when a PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, MongoDB, libSQL, Compose, or web-server backup runs manually, on schedule, or performs retention cleanup. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.1.

CVE-2026-129989.description: Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). Prior to 0.31.1, the Nixpacks publishDirectory build setting accepts shell metacharacters and is interpolated into a docker cp command executed through child_process.exec. An authenticated user with access to an application can execute arbitrary commands on the Dokploy host when triggering a Nixpacks deployment, leading to host compromise through the privileged Docker environment. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.1.

CVE-2026-109518.description:
On Debian, Ubuntu, and derivative Linux distributions, an on-path attacker who can manipulate the HTTP traffic (including a malicious mirror or proxy) between an APT client and an archive server triggered by a package install can trick the client into installing an attacker-controlled unverified package and achieve remote code execution with root privileges.



The vulnerability is caused by the reuse of hard links and requires the client to follow redirects and retry the download of package files. It requires the client to have a non-zero Acquire::Retries configuration setting; the value 3 is the default starting with Debian 12 (bookworm) and Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (Jammy Jellyfish), so older releases are unaffected in a default configuration

CVE-2026-73971.description: Music Assistant is an open-source media library manager that integrates streaming services with connected speakers. Prior to 2.8.0, parse_arguments() passes the caller-controlled return_type parameter for config/core/get_value, config/providers/get_value, and config/players/get_value to parse_value() and Python eval() when resolving type parameters in music_assistant/helpers/api.py. Any authenticated user, regardless of role, can reach these commands through the WebSocket /ws endpoint or the REST JSON-RPC /api endpoint, causing arbitrary Python code to run with the Music Assistant server process privileges before command-handler validation, even if the request later fails. A default installation requires no special configuration, and compromise can expose secrets and configuration, alter library data, and control the application container. This issue is fixed in version 2.8.0.

CVE-2026-76818.description: Axon is an agent-agnostic context engine that gives AI coding agents continuous memory across sessions, tools, and machines. Prior to 0.1.1, rtk-install in src/axon/context/rtk_bootstrap.py uses _http_download() to fetch a prebuilt rtkx release archive and _extract_binary() to mark it executable, after which compress_text_with_rtk() invokes it without verifying a checksum, signature, or build attestation. If the sammyjdev/rtkx release pipeline or maintainer release credentials are compromised, an attacker can supply a modified binary that executes with the Axon process privileges when a user installs or automatically bootstraps rtkx. This issue is fixed in version 0.1.1.

Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u511b33-perf, 17.0.21.0.3, 21.0.13.0.3, 25.0.5.0.3, 27.0.1.0.3; Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.21.0.3 and  21.0.13.0.3; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.20.0.3. Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in takeover of Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition. Note: This vulnerability can only be exploited by supplying data to APIs in the specified Component without using Untrusted Java Web Start applications or Untrusted Java applets, such as through a web service. CVE-2026-123007.description:
This issue affects NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source configurations that use HTTP/2. When NGINX processes undisclosed traffic, the flow control window can exceed the allowed threshold, potentially resulting in a heap buffer overflow typically followed by an NGINX worker segmentation fault. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact: An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to crash the NGINX worker process, corrupt its memory, or potentially execute code remotely. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-82025.description: WP File Manager before 8.0.7 contains a file upload restriction bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to upload arbitrary PHP files by exploiting a misconfigured elFinder connector in file_folder_manager.php where an empty uploadDeny list causes allowPutMime() to unconditionally return true, bypassing the uploadAllow restriction. A security vulnerability affecting Apache Roller versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 permits unauthenticated remote code execution via XML-RPC data processing.

The Apache Software Foundation confirmed this matches CVE-2026-82384.

Affected: Apache Roller 4.0.0-6.1.4.

Patch: Upgrade to version 6.1.6 or later, or apply mitigation steps for older installations.

https://en.hacks.gr/sovaro-keno-asfaleias-stin-platforma-apache-roller-epitrepei-ton-elegcho-systimaton/

#ApacheRoller #CVE202682384 #RCE #Patch

CVE-2026-82384.description: Deserialization of Untrusted Data in Apache Roller 6.1.5 allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to cause deserialization of attacker-controlled bytes, because the XML-RPC endpoint accepts vendor extension types that are deserialized during request parsing, before authentication. The servlet is mapped unconditionally, so parsing occurs even when the global XML-RPC feature is set to disabled; no non-default configuration is required for this path. This can lead to remote code execution. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later, which disables the extension types and rejects requests when the XML-RPC feature is disabled.

posts.content:
Excuse a bit of a rant, aimed in no particular direction.

I received an email from the NCSC via Netcraft last week, warning me that my Nextcloud instance contained the Apache mod_http2 vulnerability (CVE-2026-119618). They also sent the warning to Hetzner who sent me a nastygram about my responsibilities to check it out.

Here's the problem: I'm running Nextcloud in a Docker container, and the maintainers aren't in any rush to update apache to 2.4.71 any time soon.

1/3
